It’s been one year since President Biden signed the CHIPS and Science Act into law.

Here’s what you need to know.

media.alt_text:
Semiconductors power everything from cell phones to cars to refrigerators.

America invented these chips – but now we produce only 10% of them.

President Biden signed the CHIPS and Science Act to change that.

tweets.text: https://t.co/KniM0EbJFp

media.alt_text: In the year since President Biden signed the CHIPS and Science Act into law, companies have announced over $166 billion in new manufacturing investments for semiconductors and electronics.

tweets.text: https://t.co/WSUVjd3RJb
tweets.text_resolved: https://t.co/WSUVjd3RJb

media.alt_text:
At least 50 community colleges in 19 states have announced new or expanded programming to help American workers access good-paying jobs in the semiconductor industry over the past year.

And, student applications to full-time jobs posted by semiconductor companies were up 79% in 2022-2023, compared to just 19% for other industries.

We’re already making progress:
- Supporting U.S. semiconductor manufacturing
- Protecting national security and advancing global leadership
- Creating jobs and workforce pipelines for American workers
- Investing in innovation
- Supporting regional economic development and innovation 
- Supporting wireless innovation and security

Because of President Biden’s CHIPS and Science Act, America is strengthening its role in semiconductor production and innovation.

We’ll continue to implement this historic law.
